as_told.title: Thomas Townsend Brown's interest in gravity manipulation as a path to time travel

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, has talked in several episodes about T. Townsend Brown, an American inventor of the mid-1900s who built a device he called a gravitator, meant to tie electricity and magnetism to gravity. Citing a biography of Brown called The Man Who Mastered Gravity, Michels says a man named Morgan once blew up and called the device a time machine. In other episodes Michels says Brown made more progress than anyone knew, was privately obsessed with time travel, and even called himself a time traveler, and he credits Brown's daughter as a source for that, which would make Brown's work much more than an odd engine.
